list.head: Code Descriptions
list.label: a
list.item: Use for non-manuscript language material, including microforms and electronic resources that are basically textual in nature, whether they are reproductions from print or originally produced.
list.label: c
list.item: Use for printed, microform, or electronic notated music.
list.label: d

list.label: e
list.item: Use for non-manuscript cartographic material or a microform of non-manuscript cartographic material.
list.label: f
list.item: Use for manuscript cartographic material or a microform of manuscript cartographic material.
list.label: g
list.item: Use for motion pictures, videorecordings (including digital video), filmstrips, slide, transparencies or material specifically designed for projection.
list.label: i
list.item: Use for recordings of nonmusical sounds (e.g., speech).
list.label: j
list.item: Use for musical sound recording (e.g., phonodiscs, compact discs, or cassette tapes.
list.label: k
list.item: Use for two-dimensional nonprojectable graphics such as, activity cards, charts, collages, computer graphics, digital pictures, drawings, duplication masters, flash cards, paintings, photo CDs, photomechanical reproductions, photonegatives, photoprints, pictures, postcards, posters, prints, spirit masters, study prints, technical drawings, transparency masters, and reproductions of any of these.
list.label: m
list.item: Use for computer software (including programs, games, fonts), numeric data, computer-oriented multimedia, online systems or services. Other classes of electronic resources are coded for their most significant aspect (e.g., language material, graphic, cartographic material, sound, music, moving image). In case of doubt or if the most significant aspect cannot be determined, consider the item a computer file.
list.label: o
list.item: Use for a mixture of various components issued as a unit and intended primarily for instructional purposes where no one item is the predominant component of the kit. Examples are packages of assorted materials, such as a set of school social studies curriculum material (books, workbooks, guides, activities, etc.), or packages of educational test materials (tests, answer sheets, scoring guides, score charts, interpretative manuals, etc.).
list.label: p
list.item: Use for materials in two or more forms that are usually related by virtue of their having been accumulated by or about a person or body. Includes archival fonds and manuscript collections of mixed forms of materials, such as text, photographs, and sound recordings. Intended primary purpose is other than for instructional purposes (i.e., materials coded as "o").
list.label: r
list.item: Includes man-made objects such as models, dioramas, games, puzzles, simulations, sculptures and other three-dimensional art works, exhibits, machines, clothing, toys, and stitchery. Also includes naturally occurring objects such as, microscope specimens (or representations of them) and other specimens mounted for viewing.
list.label: t
list.item: This category is applied to items for language material in handwriting, typescript, or computer printout including printed materials completed by hand or by keyboard or a microform of these categories. At the time it is created, this material is usually intended, either implicitly or explicitly, to exist as a single instance. Examples include marked or corrected galley and page proofs, manuscript books, legal papers, and unpublished theses and dissertations.

elementSpec.desc: A cutout is a section of a document sheet that has been removed and is now missing.

attDef.desc: Describes the method of removing the cutout.

section is ripped off the page, leaving a rough edge.

remarks.p: The dimensions (@width, @height) of the parent element (e.g., folium) indicate the size of the bounding box of the remaining part of the page. That is, if the complete lower half of a page has been cut, the @width and @height attributes describe the remaining upper half. If, in contrast, only the lower right quarter of the page has been cut, these attributes still indicate the size of the full page (assuming that the removed section was a regular rectangle).

The dimensions (@width, @height) on cutout itself are only to be used when there is a "gap" in the manuscript that allows to specify the dimensions of that missing part. In this case, the bounding box dimensions are given, together with @x and @y to indicate the upper left point on the original page. If, however, the removed section is available by itself, then a corresponding folium (or bifolium) should be placed inside the cutout element, and should provide it’s own dimensions using @width and @height there. In this case, @width and @height on cutout is expendable.

valItem.desc: Plaine & Easie Code.
**kern representation of the Humdrum format.

Parsons code containing intervallic direction only (e.g., "sususddsdsdsd"). Permitted values are composed of a series of tokens, which may be "u" (Up), "d" (Down) or "s" (Same). Tokens should not be separated by spaces.

Representation of interval quality and direction (e.g., "P1 +P5 P1 +M2 P1 -M2"). Values must be composed of a series of space-separated tokens, where each token is comprised of three components: a direction indicator ("+" for "up" and "-" for "down"); an interval quality, being one of "P" (Perfect), "M" (Major), "m" (Minor), "A" (Augmented), or "d" (Diminished); and finally an integer indicating interval size, where "1" is a Unison. (For a Perfect Unison, P1, the direction indicator may be omitted).

Representation of intervallic direction and size in half steps (semitones) (e.g., "0 +7 0 +2 0 -2"). Values must be composed of a series of space-separated positive or negative integers indicating the number of semitones to ascend or descend, respectively.

attDef.desc: Specifies the number of written text lines per column.

remarks.p: A single number indicates that all columns have this number of written text lines. Two numbers mean that the number of text lines per column varies between the values supplied.

attDef.desc: Specifies the number of ruled staves per column.

remarks.p: A single number indicates that all columns have this number of ruled staves. Two numbers mean that the number of ruled staves per column varies between the values supplied.

attDef.desc: Specifies the number of written staves per column.

remarks.p: A single number indicates that all columns have this number of written staves. Two numbers mean that the number of written staves per column varies between the values supplied.
The model of this element is based on the layout element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Collects a set of layout descriptions.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the layoutDesc element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Controlled vocabulary term describing a page layout technique found within a resource. Analogous to MARC21 340 ǂk. If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.

sch:rule.context: mei:layoutTech[not(matches(normalize-space(.), '^(|back to back|bar by bar|bar over bar|both sides|double line spacing|double sided|line by line|line over line|melody chord system|open score|outline|paragraph|section by section|short form scoring|single line|single sided)$'))]

elementSpec.desc: Supplies the descriptive and declarative metadata prefixed to every MEI-conformant text.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The meiHead type attribute can have the value 'music' only when the document element is "mei".
The meiHead type attribute can have the value 'corpus' only when the document element is "meiCorpus".
The meiHead type attribute can have the value 'independent' only when the document element is "meiHead".

attDef.desc: Specifies the kind of document to which the header is attached, for example whether it is a corpus or individual text.

valItem.desc: Header is attached to a music document.
Header is attached to a corpus.
Header is independent; i.e., not attached to either a music or a corpus document.

remarks.p: In order to encourage uniformity in the provision of metadata across document types, this element is modelled on an element in the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI) standard. This information is often essential in a machine-readable environment. Five sub-elements must be encoded in the following order: altId(optional), fileDesc(required), encodingDesc(optional), workList(optional), and revisionDesc(optional). These elements and their sub-elements provide: a unique identifier for the MEI file, bibliographic information about the MEI file and its sources, information about the encoding process, information about the creation of the work being encoded, and statements regarding significant revisions of the file. The xml:lang attribute may be used to indicate the language in which the metadata content of the header is provided.

elementSpec.desc: Captures information about mensuration within bibliographic descriptions.
Captures information about the time signature within bibliographic descriptions.

remarks.p: This element is used exclusively within bibliographic descriptions. Do not confuse meter with the meterSig or meterSigGrp or attributes used by staffDef and scoreDef to record this data within the body of an MEI file.

elementSpec.desc: Supplies the formal name of the namespace to which the elements documented by its children belong.

attDef.desc: Formal namespace identifier; that is, a uniform resource identifier (URI).
Prefix associated with the formal identifier.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the namespace element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Indicates the extent of normalization or regularization of the original source carried out in converting it to electronic form.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the normalization element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Collects any notes providing information about a text additional to that recorded in other parts of the bibliographic description.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the notesStmt element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Any characteristic that serves to differentiate a work or expression from another.
Describes a physical writing surface attached to the original document.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The allowed positions of a patch depend on its parent element.
A patch element must contain either a folium or a bifolium element.

attDef.desc: Describes the position of the patch on the parent folium / bifolium.

valItem.desc: patch attached to outer recto side of bifolium.
patch attached to inner verso side of bifolium.
patch attached to inner recto side of bifolium.
patch attached to outer verso side of bifolium.
patch attached to recto side of folium.
patch attached to verso side of folium.

attDef.desc: Describes the method of attachment of the patch.

valItem.desc: patch is glued on surface beneath.
patch is sewn on surface beneath.
patch is pinned to the surface beneath.
patch is taped on surface beneath using an adhesive strip.
patch is attached on surface beneath using a staple.

remarks.p: A patch must always contain a folium or bifolium element. The @x and @y attributes are used to position the patch on its parent surface by indicating the upper left corner of the patch. The size of the patch is encoded using the @height and @width attributes on the child folium (or bifolium).

elementSpec.desc: Used to express the duration of performance of printed or manuscript music or the playing time for a sound recording, videorecording, etc. Analogous to MARC21 008/18-20 (visual materials) and 306 subfield ǂa.

attDef.desc: Holds a W3C duration value, e.g., "PT2H34M45.67S".

elementSpec.desc: Indicates the number and character of the performing forces used in a musical composition.

remarks.p: Arrangements are coded for the medium of the work being described, not for the original medium.

elementSpec.desc: Name of an instrument on which a performer plays, a performer's voice range, or a standard performing ensemble designation.

remarks.p: In the context of a performance resource the attribute adlib marks a resource as optional.
To indicate the tuning of an instrument, the attribute trans.diat can be used.

elementSpec.desc: Several instrumental or vocal resources treated as a group.

sch:rule.sch:assert: When labels are used, usually each perfRes or perfResList has one.

remarks.p: The function of instrumentalists or vocalists is represented by the choice of perfRes and perfResList child elements. Arrangements are coded for the medium of the work being described, not for the original medium.

elementSpec.desc: Container for information about the appearance, construction, or handling of physical materials, such as their dimension, quantity, color, style, and technique of creation.

remarks.p: Dedicatory text and title page features may also be encoded here when they are not transcribed as part of the front or back matter; i.e., when they are considered to be meta-data rather than a transcription.
The model of this element is based on the physdesc element of the Encoded Archival Description (EAD).

elementSpec.desc: Provides a description of the physical materials used by a resource; i.e., base material(s), such as paper or stone, and the surface material(s), such as ink or paint.
Container for elements used to encode physical or technical information which may affect access to or use of the resource.
Designation assigned to a resource by a music publisher, usually printed at the bottom of each page, and sometimes appearing also on the title page.

remarks.p: While it is often called a "plate number", it does not always contain numbers. The facs attribute may be used to record the location of the plate number in a facsimile image.

elementSpec.desc: Speed at which the carrier must be operated or rate at which data must be provided/consumed to produce the sound intended. Analogous to MARC21 007/03, 344 ǂc, 345 ǂb, and 347 ǂf. If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.

sch:rule.context: mei:playingSpeed[not(matches(normalize-space(.), '^(|1 7/8 ips|120 rpm|15 ips|15/16 ips|16 rpm|160 rpm|3 3/4 ips|30 ips|33 1/3 rpm|45 rpm|7 1/2 ips|78 rpm|8 rpm|[1-9][0-9]*(\.[0-9]+)?\s*(c|f|i|m|r)[p/](m|s)|[1-9][0-9]*(\.[0-9]+)?\s*(k|M)?bp(m|s))$'))]

elementSpec.desc: Relationship of the colors and tones in an image to the colors and tones of the object reproduced. Analogous to MARC21 007/10 (motion picture) and 340 $o. If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.
The cost of access to a bibliographic item.

attDef.desc: Numeric value capturing a cost. Can only be interpreted in combination with the currency attribute.
Monetary unit.

remarks.p: Best practice suggests the use of controlled vocabulary for the currency attribute, such as the ISO 4217 list of currency designators.

elementSpec.desc: Project-level meta-data describing the aim or purpose for which the electronic file was encoded, funding agencies, etc. together with any other relevant information concerning the process by which it was assembled or collected.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the projectDesc element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: The record of ownership or custodianship of an item.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the respective element of the Encoded Archival Description (EAD) and the provenance element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Container for information regarding the publication or distribution of a bibliographic item, including the publisher’s name and address, the date of publication, and other relevant details.

remarks.p: When an item is unpublished, use only the unpub sub-element.
The model of this element is based on the publicationStmt element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Controlled vocabulary term describing one or more regions of the world for which videodisc or video game carrier has been encoded, restricting playback to devices configured to decode it. Analogous to MARC21 347 ǂe. If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.

sch:rule.context: mei:regionalEncoding[not(matches(normalize-space(.), '^(|all regions|region 1|region 2|region 3|region 4|region 5|region 6|region 7|region 8|region A|region B|region C (Blu-ray)|region C (video game)|region J|region U/C)$'))]

elementSpec.desc: Controlled vocabulary term describing the clarity of detail in a digital image, expressed by measurement of the image in pixels, etc. Analogous to MARC21 347 ǂd.
Container for information about alterations that have been made to an MEI file.

remarks.p: It is recommended that changes be recorded in reverse chronological order, with the most recent alteration first.
The model of this element is based on the revisionDesc element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Contains a prose description of the rationale and methods used in sampling texts in the creation of a corpus or collection.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the samplingDecl element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Controlled vocabulary term describing the type of score used to represent a musical composition (e.g., (full) score, condensed score, table book, etc.). Analogous to MARC21 348 ǂa and 008/20 (music). If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.

sch:rule.context: mei:scoreFormat[not(matches(normalize-space(.), '^(|choir book|chorus score|condensed score|part|performer conductor part|piano conductor part|piano score|score|study score|table book|violin conductor part|vocal score)$'))]

elementSpec.desc: Describes the seals or similar external attachments applied to a resource.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the sealDesc element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Describes the principles according to which the musical text has been segmented, for example into movements, sections, etc.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the segmentation element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Groups information about the series, if any, to which a publication belongs.

remarks.p: The title sub-element records the series title, the respStmt element records the person or group responsible for the series, and the identifier element contains a series identifier. The contents element should be used when it is necessary to enumerate the content of the series, but not describe each component. The seriesStmt element is provided within seriesStmt for the description of a sub-series.
The model of this element is based on the seriesStmt element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Provides a description of the leaf or quire signatures found within a codex.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the signatures element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Controlled vocabulary term describing the number of apparent sound channels in the playback of a recording (monaural, stereophonic, quadraphonic, etc.). Analogous to MARC21 007/04, 344 ǂg (sound recording), and 007/08 (video recording). If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.

attDef.desc: Records the channel configuration in numeric form.

remarks.p: The number of apparent playback channels can differ from the number of physical channels of the recording medium, i.e., 2-track monophonic recordings. In this example, the soundChan element should record the fact that there is a single output channel, while the trackConfig element should capture the existence of two physical tracks. This element is analogous to MARC field 344 subfield g.

elementSpec.desc: Controlled vocabulary term describing the presence or absence of sound. Also, whether sound is captured on the medium or separately. Analogous to MARC21 007/05 (electronic), 007/05, 007/06 (motion picture, video recording), and 344 $i. If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.
A bibliographic description of a source used in the creation of the electronic file.

sch:assert.test: every $i in tokenize(., '\s+') satisfies substring($i,2)=//mei:*[local-name() eq 'source' or local-name() eq 'manifestation']/@xml:id or matches($i, '^([a-z]+://|\.{1,2}/)')

sch:rule.sch:assert: Each value in @target should correspond to the @xml:id attribute of a source or manifestation element or be an external URI.

remarks.p: This element contains, or references via its target attribute, a description of a source used in the creation of the electronic file. For description of a physical embodiment of an expression of a work use the manifestation element.
The data attribute may be used to reference one or more musical features found in the content of this particular source.
The model of this element is based on the source element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI) and the source element of the Encoded Archival Description (EAD).

elementSpec.desc: A container for the descriptions of the source(s) used in the creation of the electronic file.

remarks.p: This element is recommended where the MEI file is a transcription of existing music, but is not required when the data is originally created in MEI form.

elementSpec.desc: Controlled vocabulary term describing the equalization system, noise reduction system, etc. used in making the recording. Analogous to MARC21 007/12 (sound recording) and 344 ǂh. If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.

sch:rule.context: mei:specRepro[not(matches(normalize-space(.), '^(|CCIR encoded|CX encoded|dbx encoded|Dolby|Dolby Digital|Dolby Digital 1.0|Dolby Digital 2.0|Dolby Digital 5.1|Dolby-A encoded|Dolby-B encoded|Dolby-C encoded|DTS|DTS 5.0|DTS 5.1|DTS-HD Master Audio|DTS-HD Master Audio 5.1|DTS-HD Master Audio 7.1|LPCM|LPCM 2.0|NAB standard|PCM|PCM 5.1|PCM 5.1 uncompressed|PCM uncompressed)$'))]

elementSpec.desc: Describes official marks indicating ownership, genuineness, validity, etc.
Specifies the format used when standardized values are supplied; e.g., dates or numbers.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the stdVals element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Contains a phrase that specifies the hardware and/or software needed to access or use an electronic resource.
Provides detailed information about the tagging applied to a document.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the tagsDecl element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Documents the usage of a specific element within the document.

sch:rule.sch:assert: @context attribute should contain an XPath expression.

attDef.desc: Name of the element.
Circumstances in which the element appears, an XPath expression.
Number of occurrences in the defined context.
Number of occurrences in the defined context that have an xml:id attribute.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the tagUsage element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Defines a typology either implicitly, by means of a bibliographic citation, or explicitly by a structured taxonomy.
Collection of text phrases which describe a resource.

sch:rule.sch:assert: When labels are used, usually each term has one.

remarks.p: An external taxonomy from which all the descendant term elements are drawn may be referred to using the target attribute.

elementSpec.desc: Container for title and responsibility meta-data.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the titleStmt element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Controlled vocabulary term describing the number of tracks present in an audio recording or sound-track film. Analogous to MARC21 007/08 and 344 ǂe. If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.

sch:rule.context: mei:trackConfig[not(matches(normalize-space(.), '^(^(|8 track|12 track|16 track|center track|edge track|full track|half track|quarter track|[1-9][0-9]* track)$)$'))]

remarks.p: The number of apparent playback channels can differ from the number of physical channels of the recording medium, i.e., 2-track monophonic recordings. In this case, the trackConfig element should record the fact that there are two physical tracks on the sound medium, while the soundChan element should be used to state that there is a single output channel. This element may be mapped to MARC field 344 subfield ǂe or subfield ǂf as appropriate.

elementSpec.desc: A record of the treatment the item has undergone (e.g., de-acidification, restoration, etc.).

remarks.p: Treatment history may also comprise details of the treatment process (e.g., chemical solutions used, techniques applied, etc.), the date the treatment was applied, etc.
The model of this element is based on the respective element of the Encoded Archival Description (EAD).

elementSpec.desc: Scheduled treatment, e.g., de-acidification, restoration, etc., for an item.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the respective element of the Encoded Archival Description (EAD).

elementSpec.desc: Contains a description of the typefaces or related aspects of the printing of a printed resource.

remarks.p: The model of this element is based on the typeDesc element of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).

elementSpec.desc: Used to explicitly indicate that a bibliographic resource is unpublished.

remarks.p: A short phrase indicating the nature of or the reason for the unpublished status may be given as the element’s content.

elementSpec.desc: Container for information about the conditions that affect use of a bibliographic item after access has been granted.

remarks.p: useRestrict may indicate limitations imposed by an owner, repository, or legal statute (for example, copyright law) regarding the reproduction, publication, or quotation of the item. It may also indicate the absence of restrictions, such as when rights have been ceded to the public domain. Do not confuse this element with the accessRestrict element, which holds information about conditions affecting the availability of the material.
The model of this element is based on the userestrict element of the Encoded Archival Description (EAD).

elementSpec.desc: Controlled vocabulary term describing the schema, standard, etc., used to encode the video content of a resource. Analogous to MARC21 007/04 (video recording) and 346 $a. If one of the recommended values is not used, then an auth or auth.uri attribute is required.
Contains a description of the watermark(s) of an item.

Provides a detailed description of a work — a distinct intellectual or artistic creation — specifically its history, language use, and high-level musical attributes (e.g., key, tempo, meter, medium of performance, and intended duration).

remarks.p: The perfDuration element captures the intended duration of the work.

elementSpec.desc: Grouping mechanism for information describing non-bibliographic aspects of a text.

sch:rule.sch:assert: When labels are used, usually each work has one.
